steps.text: Preheat the oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). Place butter in a 9x13-inch baking dish and set it on the oven rack to melt.
Mix together flour, sugar, and baking powder in a medium bowl. Stir in milk.
Remove the baking dish from the oven as soon as butter is melted. Pour batter into the dish, but do not stir. Pour fruit evenly into the pan and do not stir.
Increase oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Bake until fruit is bubbling and cobbler is golden on top, 50 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Cherry Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This cherry cobbler is made with cherry pie filling and sweet biscuit dough for a favorite dessert. It’s delicious with fresh cherries during summer, too!
raw_recipe.name: Easy Cherry Cobbler

review.reviewBody: Wow, good old fashioned comfort dessert at its finest! And who would have ever thought something so down home good could be so easy and quick to throw together? Knowing I'm repeating many tips already suggested, this is what I found worked well: Add 1/4 tsp vanilla and a little cinnamon to the batter, bake in an 8" square pan or equivalent sized baking dish,cut butter down to 6 tablespoons, and sprinkle with sugar during the last 15 minutes of baking. Have fun with your favorite flavors of pie filling - all work well. Mmmmmmmmm, grandmas always were the best bakers, yours included, Jan!

This is the Southern recipe for any cobbler. My mother in-law mostly made it with peaches. If you want to change it up, go ahead, but please note that this is the traditional Southern cobbler recipe. They call it a cuppa, cuppa, cuppa. For one cup of each flour, milk, and sugar. They use self rising flour and not baking powder needed. Also bake at 400 degrees for about 45 minutes.

Really easy and very good - tastes like more!! I did cut the butter back to 6 T and cut the sugar down to 3/4 C. Be sure to whisk the flour, sugar, milk mixture really well to get all the lumps gone. I also added about a good tsp of cinnamon to the batter mixture - that was a good thing! Baked it in an 8x8 for 50 minutes. Gonna do this again and again!

I make this all the time with fresh peaches, I don't peel them, just slice & sprinkle a little four mixed with cinnamon on the peaches before pouring over the batted. I also sprinkle chopped pecans or walnuts on top

This recipe is delicious but definitely needs to be modified; as written is too much butter and too large of a baking dish. Using a smaller baking dish (I used a 5x8 baking dish) and half as much butter, it's absolutely perfect. It's now a go-to dessert for me because it's so easy to throw together! I've made this twice with homemade cherry pie filling and once with homemade peach pie filling. I've even made it with 1/4c coconut oil when out of butter and it was great! It's a keeper!
Used 1/2 stick of unsalted butter, and cinnamon to the batter and extra cherry pie filling because I had it. I used my Le Creuset 5 1/2 US Qt Dutch Oven. It turned out perfect.

This recipe is perfect as it is written. Yes, it has butter, it's a cobbler, come on! I doubled the recipe and baked in a 13x9 Pan for 60 minutes. I have made this with cherry, apple, blackberry, blueberry & Peach pie filling. Each time was perfect. When taking it out of the oven, I thought OMGosh there is butter pooling up there and assumed it was ruined but while it cooled the butter soaked up into the cake parts. It was AMAZING! Ignore these "butter panic'ers" and enjoy a good old fashioned cobbler!

Took several suggestions...used 6 TBS butter, 3/4 cup white sugar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tsp vanilla and 1/4 tsp allspice and baked in a 8x8 pan. Butter does pool when done, but spooned that over biscuits. Yummy!

I did reduce the butter to 6 T. and tge sugar to 3/4 cup, and added vanilla and cinnamon per previous reviews. I mixed the extra 1/4 cup sugar with flaked almonds and scattered that on top for the last 5 minutes of baking. Used a 9x9" ceramic baking dish, baked 50 minutes. Very good!

My wife made this, we used fresh cherries prepared as pie filling. We used three cups of cherries instead of two just so it had more fruit. We sprinkled some sugar on top of the crust when it was about half done baking. It turned out great. This is very easy and is definitely a keeper.

It was divine! I took note of some of the comments in this recipe. I used a 9 x 8 glass pan. I added 2 cups of flour, 1 tsp of vanilla, 1-1/2 cups milk, 2 tsp cinnamon, 2 tsp baking powder. It was absolutely delicious! I love the crispiness of the butter and sugar baked into the batter. I'll make this again and will be sure to have more vanilla ice cream!
It was delicious. We added 1 tsp of vanilla to the batter! Super easy and fast.
The temp is too low. The original recipe for lazy day cobbler (which is what this is) said 350 degrees NOT 275. I had it at 275 for over and hour and finally raised it because it wasn't getting done.
It was so very easy to make, and it was so good!
I had to make two?Because the first one was gone in ten minutes.Everybody loved it.
I added a little icing on top with just a bit of almond extract

Quite easy to make. I would probably cut back the sugar to 3/4 cup next time, but to each their own taste. Made with cherry filling, and another one with apple. As others suggested added vanilla and cinnamon.
A simple dessert done in under an hour and a half, with minimal ingredients, but tastes like a %1000 more effort was put in! Great recipe.
Ive made this recipe 4 times now with different fillings. I like to add a tsp of vanilla and it comes out delicious everytime!!
Amazing
